newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Swire sees business as usual after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK's Swire sees business as usual after handover.

text.p: As Hong Kong approaches its final month under colonial rule, one of its major British "Hongs" Swire Pacific Ltd sought on Saturday to ease fears about its future under Chinese sovereignty.
"As far as I am concerned, we believe that the playing field will be level," chairman Peter Sutch told reporters.
"I think it is business as usual."

Shares in Swire Pacific Ltd have underperformed the Hong Kong market this year amid a stampede by investors for China related stocks ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.

"There is one, I think, overwhelming factor which I think is wrong...that is the perception that as a "British Hong" perhaps we are not going to have the same level playing field post July that we have had in the past," said Sutch.
Hong is the old name for large trading houses.
"The other theory is that we have been in a 'privileged' position up until now. If we had been in a privileged position we would probably be three or four times the size we are."
Sutch said investors were likely to change their view over time. "I believe this is a perception that with time, three may be six months, will have been corrected," he said.
